reason: The description matches the implementation very closely. It correctly identifies that XMLUtil is a utility class containing whitespace skipping, XML name validation, hex-prefix detection, bounded string comparison, a simplified UTF-8/high-bit check, and declarations for BOM/entity/UTF conversion plus primitive serialization/parsing helpers and configurable boolean serialization strings. It is also appropriately framed as a class-level description rather than pretending to describe bodies for methods that are only declared here. The main gap is that some implementation-specific details are omitted or slightly generalized, such as the use of assertions on non-null inputs and nonnegative length, the mutable SkipWhiteSpace overload being just a const-cast wrapper, and the fact that the UTF-8 helper actually tests any high-bit byte rather than true continuation bytes. Still, the core behavior is accurate and sufficiently complete overall.
missing_functionality: Does not mention the explicit TIXMLASSERT checks for non-null pointers in SkipWhiteSpace and StringEqual, or for nonnegative nChar in StringEqual.
Does not mention that the non-const SkipWhiteSpace overload simply delegates to the const overload via const_cast.
Does not mention that StringEqual uses strncmp exactly.
incorrect_or_misleading_points: The description refers to UTF-8 continuation/high-bit bytes; the implementation's IsUTF8Continuation is actually just a high-bit test ((p & 0x80) != 0), not a true UTF-8 continuation-byte check.
Saying the class provides UTF-8 support is broadly fine, but most of the UTF-8-related items in this snippet are declarations only, not implemented behavior here.
